question: What does extended haplotype homozygosity measure?

answers.answer: How far along the chromosome carriers of an allele still share an unbroken, identical haplotype
answers.feedback: Correct — a sweep leaves a long shared stretch that recombination has not yet broken.

answers.answer: How many heterozygous sites an individual has
The allele frequency
answers.feedback: Frequency is what the other family of statistics uses.

answers.answer: The recombination rate
answers.feedback: That is the map, which is an input.

answers.answer: They read along a single chromosome; without phase you cannot tell which alleles sit together on the same haplotype
Because phasing removes errors
Because selscan cannot read VCFs otherwise
They do not — it only makes them faster

question: A genetic map in centimorgans is supplied rather than using physical positions. What goes wrong without it?

answers.answer: Regions of low recombination keep long haplotypes for ordinary reasons, and would look selected everywhere
answers.feedback: Correct — homozygosity has to be measured against recombination distance.

answers.answer: The positions would be in the wrong order
Nothing — the map is optional
The allele frequencies would be wrong

question: iHS is normalised within allele-frequency bins. Why is that necessary?

answers.answer: Expected haplotype length depends on allele frequency, so raw scores are not comparable between a rare and a common variant
answers.feedback: Correct — that is what the binning corrects for.

answers.answer: To make the values sum to one
To remove low-quality SNPs
To speed up the computation

question: iHS compares the two alleles at the same site; XP-EHH compares the same site between two populations. What can XP-EHH detect that iHS cannot?

answers.answer: A sweep that has gone to or near fixation, where there is no longer a contrasting allele within the population to compare against
answers.feedback: Correct — that is the reason to use a second population.

answers.answer: A sweep at very low frequency
Selection on standing variation only
Nothing — they are equivalent

question: The exercise uses the lactase region on purpose. Why is that a good choice?

answers.answer: It is a known strong recent sweep in Europeans and not in West Africans, so it is a positive control with a built-in negative
answers.feedback: Correct — CEU should show the signal and YRI should not.

answers.answer: It is the only region with phased data
It has no recombination
Because lactase is easy to sequence
